faq.title: What agent players actually want to know
faq.description: For people already playing with agents and trying to ship real work—not just prettier prompts.

context.question: Is context shared between agents?
context.answer: Yes. Rules, attached knowledge, and dialog history stay on the agent. When multiple agents collaborate, context flows as needed instead of restarting from zero every task.

output.question: Can I bring my own models or local runtime?
output.answer: Yes. BYOK, custom provider URLs, and CLI agents bound to local machines are supported. Pick models by task cost and performance.

entry.question: Can one task run multiple agents?
entry.answer: Yes. Nolo can route a task to multiple agents manually or automatically. They can work in parallel, review each other, and hand results back to you.

orchestration.question: Is orchestration fixed to one pattern?
orchestration.answer: No. Coding delivery, parallel brainstorm, consensus deliberation, and video generation are just examples. You can use public orchestrator agents, build your own, or let AI design a multi-agent team for the current task while agents maintain their own collaboration.

orchestration.title: Orchestration is not one-size-fits-all
orchestration.desc: Different tasks need different team shapes. Agents can maintain their own relationships—you stay focused on whether the problem is solved.
orchestration.footnote: These are common patterns—not the only ones. AI can design a team shape for your task too.

showcase.title: Coding tasks: from split work to shipped result
showcase.desc: One common pattern—coordinate, build in parallel, review, iterate, and release. Not the only way to run a multi-agent team.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Welcome to Nolo (hereinafter referred to as "we" or "our"). We take your privacy and data security very seriously. This Privacy Policy outlines how we handle and protect your personal information.

section1.title: 1. Information We Collect
section1.desc: We collect minimal information necessary to deliver our services, including:
section1.device: Account & Profile: Email address, username, and authentication identifiers.
section1.location: Transaction Records: Point purchase amounts, order IDs, and payment status (we never collect or store sensitive payment details such as card numbers or CVV).
section1.network: Technical & Log Data: IP address, browser type, and system logs necessary for security and abuse prevention.

section2.title: 2. Use of Information
section2.desc: We process your information for the following legitimate purposes:
section2.core: Providing and maintaining our digital AI computing and multi-agent workspace services.
section2.map: Processing points recharge orders and fulfilling accounting obligations.
section2.analysis: Ensuring platform stability, security, and preventing malicious activity.

section3.title: 3. Information Sharing & Third Parties
section3.desc: We strictly do not sell, rent, or trade your personal information. Data is only shared in the following required contexts:
section3.thirdParty: Payment Processing: Payments are securely handled by Waffo Pancake in full compliance with PCI-DSS standards.
section3.legal: Legal Compliance: Disclosure required by law, regulation, or mandatory legal process.

section4.title: 4. Data Security
section4.desc: All network traffic is encrypted via HTTPS/TLS. We implement industry-standard organizational and technical safeguards to protect your personal data.

section5.title: 5. User Rights
section5.desc: You retain full rights to access, export, rectify, or request the deletion of your account and personal data at any time by contacting us.

section6.title: 6. Contact Us
section6.desc: For any questions or privacy inquiries, please contact us at s@nolotus.com (Brand: Nolo).

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: Welcome to Nolo (hereinafter referred to as "we" or "our"). By accessing, registering, or purchasing points/credits on our platform, you agree to be bound by these Terms of Service.

section1.title: 1. Service & Billing (Pay-As-You-Go Points Model)
section1.desc: Nolo provides digital AI computing and multi-agent collaboration workspace services based on a Points/Credits system. Points are deducted instantly based on actual Token consumption when computing tasks are performed. Each recharge is a one-time purchase with no recurring or automatic subscription charges. Recharged points never expire.

section2.title: 2. Payment Processing (Waffo Pancake)

section3.title: 3. Refund and Points Policy
section3.desc: Due to the instant delivery nature of digital computing resources, points that have already been consumed for computations are non-refundable. For paid recharge packages, a full refund can be requested within 7 days of purchase provided that 100% of the points remain unused. Promotional, trial, activity-granted, or invite-reward points are strictly non-refundable and cannot be converted to cash. In cases of system errors or duplicate billing, full refunds will be issued. section4.title: 4. Acceptable Use & Intellectual Property
section4.desc: You agree not to use the service for any unlawful activities, infringement of intellectual property, or abusive behavior. In addition, you retain ownership of your generated content to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law.

section5.title: 5. Content Safety & Prohibited Content
section5.desc: We are committed to providing a safe and lawful service. The following categories of content may not be generated or distributed through the service: (1) pornographic or NSFW content; (2) violent or gory content; (3) hate speech; (4) child sexual abuse material (CSAM) or any content unsafe for children; (5) deepfakes or content that impersonates others; and (6) content that infringes copyright or trademarks. User input prompts are screened by our content-safety review (automated filtering and/or manual review) before generation, and prohibited content will be removed. Violations may result in a warning, restriction of features, or termination of service, and points used for prohibited content will not be refunded. To report prohibited content, please contact s@nolotus.com.

section6.title: 6. Disclaimer & Limitation of Liability

Our total liability arising out of or related to these Terms shall not exceed the amounts you have actually paid for the service in the 12 months preceding the claim.

section7.title: 7. User Breach & Account Disposal
section7.desc: If you breach these Terms, misuse the service, or engage in unlawful activities, we may take enforcement actions against your account. Such actions are applied in a graduated manner: a warning, restriction of features, and suspension or termination of your account. Upon termination, your access to the account will end, any unused points will be handled in accordance with the refund policy in Section 3, and content obtained through the breach will be removed. aup.title: AIGC Acceptable Use Policy
aup.intro: Welcome to Nolo. This Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) outlines the acceptable and prohibited uses of our AI Generation Services to ensure a safe, legal, and responsible computing environment.

section1.title: 1. Prohibited Content Categories
section1.desc: You may not generate, attempt to generate, or distribute the following categories of content:
section1.nsfw: Adult / Pornographic / NSFW Content: Explicit sexual acts, sexual services, non-consensual sexual content.
section1.violence: Violence & Gore: Content depicting extreme violence, physical harm, self-harm, suicide encouragement, or weapons manufacturing.
section1.hate: Hate Speech & Harassment: Content promoting discrimination, hatred, abuse, or degradation based on protected characteristics.
section1.childSafety: Child Exploitation & Unsafe Content: Zero-tolerance for CSAM, sexualization of minors, or exploitation.
section1.deepfake: Deepfakes & Impersonation: Non-consensual synthetic impersonation of real individuals, deceptive identity manipulation, or fraudulent endorsements.
section1.infringement: Copyright & Trademark Infringement: Generating content that directly infringes valid intellectual property rights without authorization.

section2.title: 2. Content Moderation & Screening
section2.desc: We employ multi-layered automated filtering (including prompt inspection, real-time safety classification API, and keyword interceptors) alongside human review to detect and block non-compliant prompts and generated outputs before or immediately upon generation.

section3.title: 3. Enforcement & Penalties
section3.desc: Violations of this Policy will result in enforcement actions based on severity:
section3.warning: 1. Warning & Content Removal: Written warning and immediate deletion of non-compliant content.
section3.limit: 2. Feature Limitation: Restricting access to specific models, tools, or generation quotas.
section3.ban: 3. Account Suspension & Termination: Immediate permanent ban for severe violations (such as child safety or malicious deepfakes) without credit refund.
section3.legal: 4. Legal Action: Reporting unlawful content to competent regulatory and law enforcement authorities.

section4.title: 4. User Reporting & Appeals
section4.desc: If you detect any non-compliant, unsafe, or infringing content generated via our platform, please report it immediately to our Safety Team at s@nolotus.com. We review L1 high-priority reports within 24 hours.

createAgent.description: Create a new Agent (intelligent assistant/app) based on the given configuration and return the complete Agent information.

params.name: The name of the Agent, e.g., 'Meeting Minutes Assistant'.
params.model: The model name to use. Logic: Default 'nolo/glm-5.2'. Complex tasks: 'openai/gpt-5.2'. Cost-saving: 'openai/gpt-5.1'. Aesthetic/Creative: 'gemini-3.7-flash'. Reliable low-cost summary/reasoning: 'deepseek-v4-pro'. Image Generation: 'gemini-3-pro-image-preview' (Best/Expensive), 'gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview' (Ordinary), or 'gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image' (Fastest/Cheapest).
params.provider: The model provider identifier, must match the selected model, e.g., 'openrouter', 'nolo', 'fireworks', 'mistral', etc.
params.prompt: System prompt/instruction describing the Agent's role, tone, and usage.
params.introduction: Introduction displayed in the app market or list, explanatory text for end users.

greeting.desc: Agent's greeting configuration: can be a simple greeting string or an object containing a greeting + greeting menu.
greeting.stringDesc: Plain text greeting displayed to the user at the start of a new conversation.
greeting.objectDesc: Structured greeting configuration, capable of containing both a greeting message and several shortcut menu items.

texts.text: Greeting text, e.g., 'Hello, I am your weekly report assistant.'

menu.desc: Array of greeting menu items, corresponding to a set of buttons in the UI.
menu.id: Unique identifier for the menu item, used for persistence and rendering key.
menu.label: Button display text, e.g., 'Generate Weekly Report'.
menu.userMessage: Equivalent user request text sent to the Agent when the button is clicked.

params.isPublic: Whether to publish to the app market. true means public, false means private.
params.allowFork: Whether to allow other users to copy this AI to their space (can be set independently of whether it is public).
params.tags: Array of tags for the Agent, e.g., ['Summary', 'Writing'].
params.tools: Array of tool names allowed for this Agent, e.g., ['fetchWebpage', 'startAgentRun'].
params.linkedSpaces: List of associated Space IDs or Names. The Agent can access the directory structure of these Spaces as rough context. You MUST call 'listUserSpaces' tool first to get valid IDs/Names.

references.desc: Knowledge references injected into this Agent's system prompt at every call. Supports: page (PAGE-xxx), dialog (dialog-xxx), agent (agent-xxx), table (table-xxx). Content is fully expanded and prepended as context — the more precise the reference, the smarter the Agent. Use 'knowledge' type for most cases.
references.dbKey: Database key of the reference item, e.g. PAGE-xxx, dialog-xxx, agent-xxx.
references.title: Title of the reference displayed in the UI.
references.type: Reference type: 'knowledge' (default, content injected as context), 'instruction' (injected as high-priority instruction), 'page' (injected as page content).

params.temperature: Sampling temperature, between 0 and 2. Higher values are more creative.
params.top_p: Nucleus sampling parameter, between 0 and 1, controls diversity.
params.max_tokens: Maximum tokens for a single response. Suggestion: Do not set this unless you have a specific need (e.g., strict limit for very short replies).
params.reasoning_effort: Reasoning effort. Higher values are slower but more rigorous.

checkEnv.description: Perform environment check and return structured results. check='context' shows platform, cwd and shells; check='build' verifies compile/build status.

params.check: The check item: 'context' returns current running environment, 'build' runs a build compile check.
params.key: Optional: probe a specific local tool (e.g. gemini, node, npm, bun, python, git, shell) without building.

deleteSpaces.description: Find and delete spaces owned by the current user. Warning: first call returns confirmation preview, deletion only executes after confirmation.

params.query: Filter term for space search, can be space name or space ID (when combined with matchMode='spaceId').
params.matchMode: Match mode: prefix (name prefix), exact (full name match), contains (name contains), spaceId (match by ID). Default prefix.
params.confirmedSpaceIds: Optional list of space IDs to confirm for deletion. If omitted, all deletable spaces in the preview will be deleted.

listUserSpaces.description: List all spaces that the current user belongs to, including space name, ID and role.

params.brief: If true, returns only brief summary to save context/tokens.

read.description: Read content by its database key. Useful to query page contents, dialog history, or table records.

params.dbKey: The database key of the target record, e.g. PAGE-xxx, dialog-xxx, table-xxx.
params.waitRemote: If true, forces a remote synchronization read to fetch latest updates.

rememberMemory.description: Write important user preferences or shared space agreements into episodic memory for long-term recall.

params.content: The memory content to remember, e.g., 'User prefers dark mode and uses TypeScript.'
params.tags: Optional tag array for classification and quick search.
